subject: SEC: 2nd-gen function env vars are readable in plaintext via Cloud Audit Logs
description: Found 2026-09-07 by the exploit auditor incidentally, while pulling updateStreak's deployment history to close BUG-268. 'gcloud logging read ... --format=json' returned that function's FULL environment variable block in plaintext, including live Discord bot/webhook credentials and HED_EXPORT_KEY. NO VALUES WERE PRINTED in her report, in any file, or in chat -- the finding is the mechanism, not the secrets. MECHANISM, and this is the part that makes it broad: Cloud Functions 2nd gen run on Cloud Run, and env vars are embedded in the Cloud Run REVISION SPEC. Cloud Audit Logs capture that spec verbatim on every deploy. So the exposure is not a misconfiguration of one function -- it is standard v2 behaviour and is very likely true for EVERY 2nd-gen function in this project. Every deploy writes another copy into the log. CONSEQUENCE: anyone holding roles/viewer or roles/logging.viewer on hexworth-prime can read production secrets without touching Secret Manager, without deploy rights, and without leaving a trace that looks like credential access. That is a much wider blast radius than the callable bugs fixed tonight, which required an authenticated student account and only ever forged that student's own XP. NOT REMEDIATED, deliberately -- this is an IAM and secrets decision, not a code change, and rotating credentials mid-session with students' progress work in flight would be reckless. THE ACTIONS, in order: (1) audit who actually holds viewer/logging.viewer on the project, since that is the real exposure surface and may be a short list; (2) confirm the scope by checking a second 2nd-gen function rather than generalising from one -- she checked updateStreak only and said so; (3) decide on rotation for the Discord credentials and HED_EXPORT_KEY, noting that rotation alone does not help while the mechanism persists, because the next deploy re-logs the new values; (4) the durable fix is moving these to Secret Manager references rather than plain env vars, so the revision spec carries a POINTER and the audit log captures the pointer instead of the secret. Track (4) as the real fix; (1) tells you how urgent it is.
